A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, figures and reference code support reliable comparison despite substantial relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original training and evaluation results for nanoGPT, Gemma, ResNet-50 and translation Transformers in Section 6 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds the Shakespeare linear-quantization comparison in Appendix A.1.11 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The three-stage quantization procedure, ridge-regression dequantization, sparsification extension, centered Hadamard transform and affine multiplication shortcut remain unchanged. The reference code is retained; the additional linear experiment uses an already defined method variant.

E1.justification: Both versions use Shakespeare, OpenWebText, C4, ImageNet and the same WMT translation datasets and language directions. Figure 9 adds a control within the existing Shakespeare task, without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 9 adds STE with linear quantization as a separate comparator alongside affine STE in the Shakespeare comparison. v2 Section 6.2 and Figure 1(a) compare against affine STE, BitNet and ParetoQ. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1.11 adds an evaluation control that restricts the proposed estimator and STE to identical symmetric linear quantization, with validation-loss trajectories over 5,000 steps. Existing benchmark splits, model sizes and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Shakespeare ablation separates estimator stability from the benefits of affine quantization. Existing Gemma quantization comparisons and analyses of Hadamard centering, sparsity, block size and regularization are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies a repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-estimation protocol for these comparisons. v3 adds no confidence intervals or significance tests, and Figure 9 reports trajectories without accompanying uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 9 newly reports Shakespeare validation loss of approximately 2.1 for the proposed linear variant versus above 5.0 for linear STE, with the affine variant reaching approximately 1.9. Tables 1–13 retain their numerical results, and v2's OpenWebText Figure 6 is retained as v3 Figure 8.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4, Equations 10–13, derives the linear dequantizer's local Jacobian and its data-dependent rank-one correction, explicitly relating it to quantization error. This is a bounded extension of the analysis; the ridge objectives, affine-shortcut theorem and proof, and complexity analysis are retained.

C1.justification: v2 presents the missing corrective gradient as a proposed primary source of instability. v3's abstract, introduction and summary more categorically identify it as the key issue and claim its identification for the first time. The contributions concerning low-bit training, sparsity, the affine shortcut and efficiency frontiers remain.

C2.justification: The new ablation discussion explicitly attributes stability gains to the estimator independently of affine quantization. Sections 2.3 and 6.4.2 also shift emphasis from bridging artificial and biological intelligence toward practical low-bit hardware and an alternative to spiking networks. Existing energy-proxy limitations remain.

D1.justification: The shortened Section 6.1 removes v2's explicit statement that all transformer experiments use AdamW with cosine scheduling and warmup. Frameworks, hardware, default block size, regularization and reference code remain documented. This reduces implementation disclosure without establishing an actual training-setting change.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Gallego et al. (2020) and Tavanaei et al. (2019) citations and references while shortening the biological motivation. It strengthens positioning around gradients without surrogate estimation, while retaining the substantive comparisons with ParetoQ, QuEST and STBLLM.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are substantially rewritten, accompanied by revisions across the introduction, biological motivation, experimental setup and scaling discussion. The appendix gains an expanded roadmap and moves related work from its beginning to near its end, producing broad narrative and organizational changes.

P2.justification: v2's four-panel Figure 1 becomes v3 Figure 1 plus separate, enlarged efficiency-frontier Figures 2 and 3. The two scaling panels are enlarged and stacked in Figure 4. Appendix displays are rearranged, captions expanded and Figure 9 added; the existing plotted data are retained.

improvement.justification: Figure 9 supplies a control missing from v2's Shakespeare comparison, improving support for estimator gains independently of affine quantization. Enlarged efficiency plots also improve readability. These benefits provide a limited net improvement, tempered by lost optimizer/schedule details and the new Equation 13's omission of the transform's direct dependence on x, which limits the completeness of the strengthened gradient argument.
